To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a physical map of the 8p22 deletion interval has been prepared that includes the position of the markers in relation to each other, the position of the marker in relation to the larger chromosomal context has been confirmed using RH mapping, and six unique expressed sequences have been identified that map to the interval.
a physical map of the deletion region was prepared, that a transcript map was constructed, and that the transcript map includes two known genes and six novel EST sequences.

a high-resolution BAC contig of a prostate cancer 8p22 interval has been assembled, that the position of the selected BACs across the interval was confirmed by RH, and that the contig and RH map was used to identify six transcribed units that might represent candidate genes for the prostate tumor suppressor gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying and isolating the genes that might underlie prostate cancer progression.
the identification and characterization of a candidate prostate tumor suppressor gene on 8p21-22.
the identification of the tumor suppressor gene in the prostate cancer deletion interval of 8p22.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the physical map and the identification of transcription units within the deletion interval have provided a foundation for further studies of the prostate cancer deletion region of 8p22.
the physical and transcript map of the 8p22 deletion interval has been completed and that the next step is to test for the loss of these genes in prostate tumors.
the physical map of the 8p22 interval has been established and the transcription units within this interval have been defined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the physical map of the 8p22 deletion interval is now complete and the transcriptional map of the interval has been extended.
we have constructed a physical map of the 8p22 deletion interval and identified several potential transcription units that may be associated with the prostate tumor suppressor gene.
the physical map is now complete, the position of the markers on the RH scale has been confirmed, and a transcript map is available for the deletion interval.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to assemble a complete bacterial contigt across a 1-Mb region of human chromosome 8, and to integrate the contig into the RH database.
a combination of physical mapping and transcript identification can be used to identify genes within a deletion interval.
the use of RH mapping, BAC contigs, and ESTs can be used to identify and characterize a deletion interval that is a candidate site for a prostate cancer tumor suppressor gene.
